title: INDEX: a value at a row and column

screens.prompt: In B7, read the units at the row in B5 and the column in B6, counting from the first product and from Q1.

hints.syntax: =INDEX(B2:D4,B5,B6): the block, then the row and column counts from its top-left corner.
hints.func-index: INDEX needs a block with both height and width. Given B2:D4 it can return any of the nine figures.
hints.require-ref: Take the row and column from B5 and B6. Typing 3 and 2 freezes the answer to Gizmo's Q2.
hints.value: Three rows down from B2 is row 4, Gizmo. Two columns across is Q2, and the figure there is 160.
hints.error: Column 9 in a block three columns wide is outside it, and the cell shows #REF!.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
two arguments read along the first column only, so the column in B6 is ignored
the row number is not a product name, so there is nothing for VLOOKUP to search
that reads row 3, column 3, which is Gizmo's Q3 figure of 150
the row and column typed into the formula, so the reader cannot ask for a different cell
column 9 is outside a block that is only three columns wide, so INDEX returns #REF!

docs.explain:
INDEX reads one cell out of a rectangular block. The block is B2:D4, so Widget's Q1 sits at B2, which is position 1, 1. Counting three rows down and two columns across lands on C4, which holds 160. The result goes in B7.

The count restarts at the top-left corner of whatever range you hand it. Row 1 of the block is sheet row 2, and column 1 is column B, so the 3 and 2 in B5 and B6 count from B2.

Feed those numbers from cells and the same formula follows the question. Change B6 to 3 and B7 reads 150, Gizmo's Q3. Change B5 to 2 and it reads 110, Gadget's Q2. Type 3 and 2 into the formula and B7 keeps answering for a cell nobody asked about.

errors.text: The row or column number points outside B2:D4, as when 9 is asked for from a three-column block.
The row or column argument arrived as text, which INDEX cannot count with.
B5 and B6 went in as column then row, so the formula reads Widget's Q3 at 130 and no error appears.

docs.atWork: Reading one quarter of one product out of a sales grid, with the quarter picked from a drop-down.
docs.outcome: Read any single cell of a grid from a row number and a column number.

seo.title: INDEX in Excel: a row and a column
seo.description: Row 3, column 2 of the block starting at B2 is 160. INDEX counts from the corner of the range you give it, so the formula follows the cells that change.
